change: six AP Cyber 1.4 and 1.5 columns were priced at numbers their students were never served, worst of them an exercise priced 4 while 46 students were served 24
_context: Found by /api/health prices on its first live read, 2026-09-07, not by a person.
That block was added the day before because a teacher had to read her own
gradebook carefully to notice the same shape on 1.1. Nobody reported these six.
Three sources agree on 24 for every one of them, which is the bar this table
needs after the 1.1 exercise-2 price was authored off a single bad read:
the page arithmetic   updateTotals/upd sum EVERY part into the element the
score reporter scrapes, and it renders "/ 24"
the ledger            24, across 314 students on the six columns
The middle source is the one an earlier crude sweep got wrong: it matched
"/ 24" in neighbouring markup and could not tell a PART total from a WHOLE
one, so it was refused as evidence at the time. Reading the routine that
writes the scraped element is what settles it.

checks.name: the six are priced 24 and each is recorded as a correction naming what it replaced
a correction lands on a stale row, leaves a hand edit alone, and regrades nobody
re-pricing cannot move a score already recorded
a correction that fires whatever the stored row says
checks._why: The from value is what stops a correction clobbering a price an operator authored by hand. Six new corrections make that guard carry six times the weight it did yesterday.
checks.expect_failure: an operator value of 12 survives the seed

checks.name: a correction that disagrees with the table it corrects
checks._why: POINTS and CORRECTIONS are two statements about one column. If they can disagree, a re-run flips the value back and forth forever and the gradebook changes under a teacher every deploy.
checks.expect_failure: a POINTS value that contradicts its correction throws

checks.name: production prices all six at 24, so none is still reported as disagreeing
checks._why: Before this deploy /api/health named all six: 1.4 at 25/25/30, 1.5 at 4/4/30, against 24 in every case. The block reporting them is the check; it cannot pass by accident.

checks.name: and the boot seed says it corrected exactly the six
checks._why: A correction that silently did nothing looks identical to one that ran. Six rows move on this deploy and none on the next, which is the idempotence claim measured rather than asserted.
